gallery_probe_convention: stem '1' = gallery (image index 00); stems '2'..'10' = probes (image indices 01-09)
christina_feature_dimension_note: Her enhanced-RL feature is 576-dim on this data (12 histogram bins + 2 row-stat values + 4 spatial values = 18 per pseudo-scale/row x 32 rows = 576). This equals the paper's stated 576-dim RL feature only by numerical coincidence (paper: 18 pure run-length histogram bins/row, C=9, x 32 rows) -- the feature composition is NOT the same (histogram + row-stats + spatial vs. pure run-length histogram).

christina_pseudo_scales.finding: extract_iris_code() vstacks Open Iris's 2 Gabor-filter scales (each (16,256,2) -> (16,512) after channel-concat) into ONE (32,512) 2D array. compute_template_features() then sets n_scales = iris_code.shape[0] == 32, so it treats the template as 32 independent 1-row pseudo-scales (scale_0..scale_31), NOT as 2 Gabor scales of 16 rows each. This is what her own enroll_identity/identify_cascading code does with real Open Iris output -- unmodified here, and preserved by NOT reshaping the saved (32,512) arrays.
christina_pseudo_scales.weight_coverage: FilterFHEConfig only defines weight_hist_scale0 (=0.50) and weight_hist_scale1 (=0.20) -- there is no weight_hist_scale2..31. In compute_l1_distance_plaintext, the assignment is positional by loop index, not a per-scale config lookup: `hist_weight = config.weight_hist_scale0 if idx == 0 else config.weight_hist_scale1`. So pseudo-scale 0 (row 0) gets weight_hist_scale0, and EACH of the other 31 pseudo-scales (rows 1-31) individually gets the SAME weight_hist_scale1 (not divided among them) -- their total effective weight (31 x 0.20 = 6.20) dwarfs row 0's (0.50). weight_row and weight_spatial are single global scalars applied once to the mean of row/spatial diffs pooled across all 32 pseudo-scales, so those two terms already treat every pseudo-scale equally.
